name: techword-code
description: Techword Code is an approval-first coding agent powered by Techword API.

techwordCode.maxToolOutputChars.description: Maximum characters returned by a workspace or terminal tool.

techwordCode.showCostInUsd.description: Show the usage counter as an estimated cost in USD instead of a raw token count. Uses the same token total, converted with the rate below.

techwordCode.usdPerMillionTokens.description: Estimate price in USD per 1,000,000 tokens. Used only as a fallback before your key's real spend meter is read (or if that meter is unavailable). Default (1.6111) matches about $5.00 per 3,103,392 tokens; change it if your provider's pricing differs.

techwordCode.usageMeterInCents.description: Whether your provider's billing meter (dashboard/billing/usage) reports spend in cents (the usual convention: $5.00 shows as 500) rather than dollars. Leave on unless the cost counter reads 100x too high, then turn it off. The exact meter value is shown in the counter's hover tooltip.

enumDescriptions: Automatically summarize earlier work and keep going when the context fills up.
Ask before summarizing so you can approve continuing.
techwordCode.contextMode.description: What to do when the conversation nears the context limit.

techwordCode.openFilesInEditor.description: Open files in the editor as Techword Code reads and edits them, so you can watch the work.

techwordCode.maxSteps.description: Maximum tool steps per task before pausing for a safety check. Raise it for very large, long-running tasks (e.g. overnight builds).

techwordCode.maxTokens.description: Maximum tokens the model may generate per reply. If a reply is cut off it continues automatically, but raising this reduces how often that happens on very large file rewrites.

techwordCode.temperature.description: Model creativity. 0 is the most focused/deterministic (best for coding); higher is more varied. Ignored while Show Thinking is on.

techwordCode.showThinking.description: Show the model's real reasoning in the Activity panel as it works. Off by default: some providers mishandle extended thinking alongside tool use, which can make the agent describe steps without carrying them out. Turn on only if your provider fully supports extended thinking. Falls back automatically if it doesn't.

techwordCode.thinkingBudget.description: How many tokens the model may spend reasoning per turn when Show Thinking is on. Higher means deeper reasoning but more tokens used.

techwordCode.enableWebFetch.description: Allow the agent to fetch web pages (docs, npm) with the web_fetch tool. Turn off to keep it fully offline.

techwordCode.customInstructions.description: Standing instructions added to every task (coding style, conventions, do/don't). Applied on top of any AGENTS.md in the repo.

techwordCode.contextTokenLimit.description: Approximate token size at which Techword Code compacts the conversation to keep working.

techwordCode.deniedGlobs.description: Workspace paths that Techword Code will not read.

techwordCode.blockedCommands.description: Extra command patterns (regex or plain text) that always require your manual approval and can never auto-run, on top of the built-in safety list (rm -rf, disk format, force push, curl | sh, sudo, etc.).

techwordCode.checkForUpdatesOnStartup.description: Check for a newer Techword Code version shortly after VS Code starts. When a newer build exists you'll be offered a one-click update.

techwordCode.autoUpdate.description: Automatically download and install a newer Techword Code version when one is found, then offer to reload. When off, you're asked first before anything is installed.

techwordCode.updateUrl.description: Override the update server URL (the latest.json endpoint). Leave blank to use the built-in Techword release server.

techwordCode.mcpServers.markdownDescription: External MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to connect. Each key is a server name; each value has a `command`, optional `args`, `env`, `cwd`, and `disabled`. Their tools become available to the agent (approval-gated) as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Example: `{ "filesystem": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "."] } }`

command.description: Executable to launch the server (e.g. npx, node, python, uvx).

env.description: Extra environment variables for the server process.

cwd.description: Working directory for the server process.

disabled.description: Set true to keep the server configured but not start it.

scripts.test: npm run check && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json && node --test "dist-test/test/**/*.test.js"
